en: What does “it’s raining cats and dogs” mean?
Pets are falling from the sky.
It is only drizzling a little.
This idiom describes a really heavy downpour. No animals are involved!
Help people relax when they first meet.
Breaking the ice means getting a conversation going so people feel comfortable.
What does “a piece of cake” mean?
If a test was a piece of cake, it was no trouble at all.
Someone who is under the weather is not feeling well.
What does “let the cat out of the bag” mean?
Letting the cat out of the bag means telling something that was meant to stay secret.
To hit the books is to settle down and study.
What does “once in a blue moon” mean?
Something that happens once in a blue moon hardly ever happens.
What does “cost an arm and a leg” mean?
If something costs an arm and a leg, it costs a huge amount of money.
Being on cloud nine means feeling wonderfully happy.
Hold your horses means slow down and do not rush.
What does “the ball is in your court” mean?
It is your turn to decide or act.
When the ball is in your court, the next move is up to you.
What does “bite off more than you can chew” mean?
Take on more than you can manage.
This means agreeing to do too much and then struggling to cope.
Spilling the beans means revealing information that was supposed to be private.
Become nervous and want to back out.
People get cold feet when they lose their nerve just before doing something.
What does “see eye to eye” mean?
Two people who see eye to eye share the same opinion.
What does “a storm in a teacup” mean?
A big fuss about something small.
A sudden spell of bad weather.
A storm in a teacup is a lot of upset over something unimportant.
What does “barking up the wrong tree” mean?
Looking for an answer in the wrong place.
A dog that has got lost.
If you are barking up the wrong tree, your guess or search is mistaken.
What does “get the ball rolling” mean?
To get the ball rolling is to make a start on something.
What does “keep an eye on” mean?
Keeping an eye on something means watching over it.
The final problem that makes someone lose patience.
The last straw is one small extra thing that is finally too much.
Someone in hot water has done something that will get them told off.
What does “every cloud has a silver lining” mean?
Something good can come from a bad situation.
This saying reminds us that even bad times can bring something good.
If you are pulling my leg, you are joking and trying to fool me.
What does “turn over a new leaf” mean?
Start behaving in a better way.
Turning over a new leaf means making a fresh start and improving.
What does “like a fish out of water” mean?
You feel like a fish out of water when you are somewhere that feels strange to you.
What does “the early bird catches the worm” mean?
People who start early get the best chances.
Birds only eat in the morning.
It is better to sleep in late.
This saying means that being early or quick gives you an advantage.
Something that will happen very soon.
Pigs cannot fly, so when pigs fly means never.
What does “in the same boat” mean?
People in the same boat are facing the same problem.
In a risky situation where trouble is close.
If you are on thin ice, one more mistake could get you into trouble.
What does “sit on the fence” mean?
Someone sitting on the fence will not say which side they agree with.

example.q_en: What does “it’s raining cats and dogs” mean?
example.why_en: This idiom describes a really heavy downpour. No animals are involved!

en.title: Idioms
en.teach: An idiom is a phrase whose meaning is different from its words. “Break a leg” means good luck, not an injury!
